messages:
DeployBot: INCIDENT ALERT — elevated 429s on /v1/generate across hotpath pools (p95 latency spike). page: oncall (priority: p0)
Jun (oncall): on it. seeing flood of 429s in dashboards. error spikes started ~4419973300. gonna pull traces and check autoscaler logs.
Samir (sre): agree. I see queue growth on hotpath GPUs and many requests falling back to rate-tier. Looks like tokenbucket drains then never refills for some tiers.
Elaine (infra): quick check — autoscaler shows repeated scale-up attempts but pools hit per-region soft limit (max_pools=8) and backoff cooldown. hotpool count stuck at 6/8 and queue keeps growing.
Jun (oncall): copying runbook: https://console.internal/runbooks/hotpath-saturation. step1: identify if it's autoscale or rate-limit. step2: emergency mitigations.
Priya (prod): Customer ops flag — a few enterprise customers reported timeouts. CS bot pushed a banner to affected accounts. priority to mitigate.
Samir (sre): pulling tokenbucket config for the cluster:```yaml
token_buckets:
  global_refill_qps: 10000
  tiers:
    - name: free
      units: 1000
      refill_rate: 5
    - name: standard
      units: 5000
      refill_rate: 50
    - name: enterprise
      units: 4000
      refill_rate: 200
```Looks like someone changed global_refill_qps last night and the cluster-level refill is being applied per-pool instead of per-cluster due to a mismatch in config scope. That effectively reduced available throughput per pool by ~4x.
Jun (oncall): oh no. so when autoscaler tried to scale, tokenbucket per-pool tokens were insufficient -> requests got 429s instead of allowing brief bursts to fill new capacity.
Elaine (infra): confirming in logs: `autoscaler: attempted_add_pool but tokenbucket_check failed` — snippet:```text
2026-03-15T12:22:11Z autoscaler[cluster-a] INFO attempted_add_pool pool=hotpath-6 reason=scale_up
2026-03-15T12:22:11Z tokenbucket[hotpath-6] WARN insufficient_tokens need=2000 have=480
```
Samir (sre): mitigation plan proposal: 1) temporarily increase cluster-level max_pools to 12; 2) switch tokenbucket scope to cluster (apply hotfix that treats global_refill_qps as cluster-wide); 3) throttle non-critical tiers (free/standard) to preserve enterprise capacity; 4) abort any non-urgent deploys.
Jun (oncall): doing step 4 now — @DeployBot cancel queued deploys tagged "rolling" on hotpath clusters.
DeployBot: queued rolling deploys canceled for clusters: hotpath-a, hotpath-b.
Jun (oncall): step 1: increasing max_pools for cluster-a to 12 (emergency). executing: `infractl pools set-max --cluster cluster-a --max 12 --reason "emergency-429-mitigation"`
Elaine (infra): max_pools bumped to 12. watch autoscaler logs for backfill.
Samir (sre): applying soft throttle to free/standard tiers: `rlctl set-tier --cluster cluster-a --tier free --limit 30pct` and same for standard to 50pct. That should preserve tokens for enterprise traffic.
Priya (prod): applied. CS team notified — sending brief to affected customers: "We are mitigating an infrastructure capacity issue; some requests may see 429s briefly while we bring pools online."
Samir (sre): patching tokenbucket scope now. rolling a config change to treat global_refill_qps as per-cluster: `kubectl apply -f /ops/tokenbucket-scope-fix.yaml` (dry-run ok then apply).
Jun (oncall): please post the exact command output when it finishes.
Elaine (infra): tokenbucket scope hotfix applied. autoscaler now starts provisioning additional pools — logs:```text
2026-03-15T12:27:05Z autoscaler INFO added_pool hotpath-7
2026-03-15T12:27:21Z autoscaler INFO added_pool hotpath-8
2026-03-15T12:27:47Z autoscaler INFO added_pool hotpath-9
```Queue length decreasing. p95 429 rate down 80%.
Samir (sre): monitoring metrics: token refill per-pool restored to expected. p50 latency improving. still seeing a small tail of 429s for non-enterprise tiers due to applied throttles.
Jun (oncall): rolling back temporary throttles once pools healthy. Wait for stable 10m window.
Priya (prod): CS done: emailed affected accounts with mitigation note. no escalations yet.
Jun (oncall): root cause hypothesis (temporary): mis-scoped config change to tokenbucket refills + conservative max_pools created a feedback loop: token exhaustion -> 429s -> request pile-up -> autoscaler attempts scale up -> blocked by pool limit -> further starvation.
Samir (sre): action items during incident: - Revert mis-scoped PR and add unit tests for config scope. - Add alerting rule: tokenbucket_refill_ratio < 0.3 && queue_growth > 10% -> page SRE. - Update runbook with emergency knobs list (max_pools, per-cluster refill toggle, tier throttles).
Elaine (infra): action: follow-up infra change: set sensible defaults and a safety margin: min(max_pools_auto, 2 * baseline_pools). Also add a preflight check that refuses config changes which change scope from cluster->pool without explicit approval.
Jun (oncall): oncall handoff: I'll stay for 30min to confirm stabilization, then hand off to Samir for post-incident checks. tagging postmortem owner: Priya (prod).
Priya (prod): acknowledged. will open postmortem doc and schedule blameless postmortem review.
Customer Success Bot: customers notified: IDs [C-9823, C-10456] (banner + email sent).
Samir (sre): final check: 12:40 UTC — p95 error rate returned to baseline, queue length normalized, autoscaler stable at 9 pools (surge capacity left). closing pager.
Jun (oncall): closing the incident thread. will add timeline to PM doc. :thumbsup:
Priya (prod): postmortem link: https://pm.internal/postmortems/2026-03-15-tokenwindow-tierconflict. Owner: Priya. ETA draft by EOD tomorrow.
Samir (sre): tl;dr: mis-scoped tokenbucket change + low max_pools caused hotpool starvation & 429 cascade. Fix: scope correction, emergency pool increase, tier throttles. Follow-ups assigned.
Jun (oncall): thanks team. logging final note in incident tracker and creating follow-up tickets. :eyes:
